newsitem.title: USA: Female Health takes Q4 inventory writedown.
newsitem.headline: Female Health takes Q4 inventory writedown.

text.p: Female Health Co said on Tuesday that it took a fiscal 1996 fourth quarter writedown of $950,000 to cover a reduction in the expected value of some of the company's inventory of female condoms.
The inventory writedown reflects historical rates of sale and on-hand inventory levels of dated product, the company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
In 1994, the company's female condom was granted a two- year product life by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and in July 1995, the FDA extended its useful life to three years.
The FDA recently notified the company verbally that it will extend the product's useful life to four years and is considering a useful life of more than four years, according to the filing.
A Female Health spokesman said that if the FDA extends the useful life, some of the product would be usable and the writedown might be revised. "There is a potential upside there," he said.

Looking ahead, Female Health said it intends in 1997 to distribute the female condoms to developing countries based on its agreement with a United Nations program on AIDS; promote the condom through television, print and the Internet; finalize contracts with international distributors; and increase sales and lower production costs.
To pursue these plans, Female Health said it will seek financing in 1997 through a debt or equity offering.

Earlier today, Female Health reported revenues of $2.1 million and a net loss of $8.7 million or $1.31 a share for its fiscal year ended September 30, 1996. This compares with revenues of $2.2 million and a net loss of $8.4 million or $1.39 for the fiscal year ended September 30, 1995.
Female Health owns certain worldwide rights to the female condom including patents which have been issued in the U.S., Japan, the European Union, China, Canada, Brazil, and Australia.
Shares of Female Health closed unchanged from Monday at 4-1/16.
